text: About time. Our men are just coming. We'll detonate by radio beam. Right, hurry it up.
Any information on that beacon signal yet? No, sir. There's been no response to the secondary emergency circuits either.
No, there wouldn't be. Sir? What do you think has happened to that beacon?
Well, it's difficult to say, sir. It could be a failure in the solar energy store.
No, the emergency power would operate and we'd get a mayday signal. Well.
Oh, you don't think this is a mechanical failure, sir? No, no, I don't.
These beacons are practically foolproof. You've got any ideas?
Yes, I have. And I must be right. Argonite. These beacons are almost entirely constructed of argonite.
What are you going to do about it? Attention, all personnel. This is General Hermann.
Your B-ship is now 50 days and many billions of miles out from Earth.
You are entering the fourth sector of our galaxy.
In this sector, for some time now, Earth's government has been aware that a highly organized gang of criminals has been roaming the spaceways and preying upon defenseless cargo ships.
The main target of these criminals is argonite, the most valuable mineral known to man, and so far only found on the planets of the fourth sector.
A government space beacon marking the approaches to the planet Eucerum has ceased transmitting.
It's navigation signals. These beacons, as you know, are constructed of argonite.
It is my belief that the criminals are attacking the government navigation beacons and plundering the argonite.
There can be no other explanation for its failure.
This being the case, I have decided to abandon our present mission and to investigate the missing beacon in the new Cerum sector.
I want all section commanders on the bridge at 20 o'clock.
We will be there in 50-100 hours, Sector 4, solar time.
Resume normal duties until then.
There are 18 space beacons scattered across this sector, sir.
Seventeen, Ian, until the one in Eucerum is replaced.
Seventeen. And they're millions of miles apart.
So how can we be sure which one the pirates are likely to attack next?
We can't.
Well, exactly. The odds are 17 to 1 against us being in the right place at the right time.
Ah. With our speed, I think we can cut those odds a bit.
Now.
There are four beacons in the Pliny solar system here.
That is where we'll start our patrol.
Speed it up.
Captain, I don't like this.
Nobody's asking you to like it. Just get those scissor charges laid into position.
If we attack any more beacons, we'll have the whole of the interstellar space core in this sector.
Look. As of this moment, the space core has its hands full of trouble.
Brush firewalls in three different sectors. There's never been a better time for getting rich.
Find that, sir. Now we'll lay four charges along the main axle.
And then we'll attach booster charges around the hull.
Okay.
You're a good engineer, Dervish. Just do your job and leave the space core to me, eh?
Okay.
But I worked ten years for Earth Government. You should have stayed with them. They'd have given you a pension.
Attacking government property is one crime they make sure never pays.
Sixteen hundred tons of pure argonite pays all right, Dervish. To me, this is like a floating bank.
What range do the four scanners set for, Pan?
Fifteen hundred, sir.
Well, we set them at two thousand, right?
Keep a sharp eye on that screen. There are lots of rogue asteroids in the planet system.
Oh, and one thing more. Make sure the minnow ships are fully fueled. And put the detonation heads on their missiles. Report back as soon as that is done.
We're approaching the planet system now, sir. We've made scanner contact with the four beacons. They're functioning normally.
Ah, good.
Well, this, the planet Tar here, is the main one in the system. We'll orbit here for a few weeks and see what happens.
So that's Tar, huh?
Have you heard of it?
Yeah. It's the headquarters of the Izigri Numani Company, the most productive planet in the entire galaxy.
Hmm. Madeleine Izigri has built quite a place there, which is one reason for basing ourselves in the planet system.
Why is that a reason, sir?
Well, if we're out here long, Ian, the men will need somewhere for rest and recreation. Deep space sickness is the one thing we can't chance.
Major Warne.
What is it, sir?
I've got a contact, sir, at beacon Alpha 7.
Well, hold on. Any identification?
No, sir. Too far away.
Ah, it's a spaceship, right enough. Check central flight information, Ian, and see if anyone should be out there.
Right, sir.
Change course for beacon Alpha 7. A bridge to power room. I want ten seconds main boost.
According to flight information, sir, there should be no ships in the area within the next 17 days.
Ah, well, whoever they are, they've not yet reported to central flight information.
You think it's the Pirates?
It could be. Though some of these commercial flights don't always like to report their whereabouts for reasons of their own. Anyway, we shall soon know.
That's yours, sir.
Keep track of her.
She's moving quite fast, sir.
She's got a good turn of speed for a commercial.
Is beacon Alpha 7 still functioning?
Yes, sir. Very strong signals now.
Maybe they were just picking up emergency supplies, sir. Some of these beacons do carry a reserve medical and oxygen equipment.
Sir, I've got another signal coming in now. It's a UHF.
UHF? But that's reserved for demolition teams.
Well, put it on audio.
Yes, sir. Alpha 7's broken up, sir.
Ah, right. I thought I'd know this.
Main boost.
Lost the beacon, sir. There are more signals.
No, there won't be. She's probably in a dozen separate beds by now.
Then hold contact with that pirate ship.
Yes, sir.
At least we can be sure they don't get away.
Ian, give me a projected arrival time.
Three hours, sir. Maybe I can get a visual on the main scanner.
There she is, sir. And that's what's left of the beacon.
Oh, you've got them cold, Ian. We'll be up to them long before they get rid of that salvage crap.
Yeah, provided she doesn't see us approaching, sir.
That ship looks fast.
They don't know we're in the same area. What's wrong with the scanner?
The ship will be losing visual contact, sir.
The ship's moving away, sir.
What?
Just started to go, and the beacon debris is going with her.
Hold back contact, Pim.
It's no good, sir. She's going too fast.
They must have twice our speed.
Maybe the minnows could hold her.
Not at this distance. They haven't the fuel.
Lost contact, sir.
Oh, hold the same course. Keep searching.
They must have attached rocket units to the beacon so the wave moved off.
Yes. They're very well organized.
They cut the beacon into several manageable pieces by means of scissor jobs.
Then shoot the bits off to some prearranged collection point. Very clever.
And quick. It cuts down the time they're at risk.
And they just burn out the argonite at their leisure.
Ian, we shall have to rethink our tactics.
We shall never catch them by normal patrol method.
What else can we do, sir?
Man the beacons.
Man them?
It's the only answer. We'll drop small parties of four or five men on each beacon.
Give them rations and supplies for two months.
Well, all these Mark 5 beacons were designed as emergency survival centers.
Yes, sir. But I don't think anybody's ever tried living on them.
Some of these beacons are pretty primitive.
I'm not interested in men's comfort, Major. Set course for the nearest beacon.
Yes, sir.
Here's your radio, Lieutenant. It's beamed automatically to main control.
All you have to do in the event of trouble is press this button, right?
Don't worry. I'll press it.
Remember, your main job here is to give us the earliest possible warning in the event of the pirate ship approaching, right?
And after that, we fight them.
I think you'll have to, Joe.
Good luck.
And to you. See you in about six weeks.
I hope.
Course for Alpha 9.
Very good, sir.
I told Lieutenant Sauber we'd be back in about six weeks, sir.
Oh, much earlier if the pirates raid Alpha 4. How's morale on the picket?
Oh, it's pretty high, sir. I think they're hoping for the chance of a party.
They understand they have to shoot on sight?
Yes, sir. I told them.
No? Anybody poking their nose aboard Alpha 4 will find plenty of trouble waiting for him.
Now, we're going to be here for about six weeks.
Settle down and keep your eyes open. Take care about everything.
Sir.
What? What are you doing here? Why aren't you in the observation tower?
There's something in the computer bay, sir.
Something? What do you mean by that?
I heard something in there, sir. A noise.
All right. We'd better check it out, then. Come on.
Oh, dear.
What's wrong?
Well, I don't think we're quite where I expected.
Never mind. This looks very interesting.
Interesting? A piece of old machinery?
Yes, I know.
I've never seen a computer quite like this before, Jamie.
It looks like some sort of control room.
Yes, but what does it control?
Well, I think we'd better get out of here before somebody catches us.
Good idea. There's a door here.
No, Zoe. I meant in the TARDIS.
Jamie, stop worrying. There's obviously nobody here.
How do you know that?
Well, this machine is programmed to operate by itself.
Yes, but what does it do?
Well, I'm not sure, Zoe, but I think we're on an unmanned spacecraft in a fixed orbit.
We're too far away from anywhere to be a weather satellite.
Let's see what clues we can find through here, Zoe.
What's that?
Stop it!
Nobody here, eh?
There's only one thing we can do. Run!
Well, maybe next time you'll listen to me.
If there is a next time.
All right. There are only three of them, and they can't get away.
Hunt them down, and don't forget, shoot to kill.
Alpha-4. Another present from the home planet's taxpayers.
Same procedure as last time?
Yes, Delwich, but now that you've had a little practice, get those scissor charges laid a bit quicker, eh?
Captain! Those are blaster guns!
Get the crew in here at the double.
You all right, Zoe?
Yes, I think so.
That should hold them for a little while.
Why are they trying to kill us? We haven't done anything.
No, no, but we're certainly not stopping to find out.
What's that?
Look!
Come on, let's find somewhere else to hide.
What do we have in here?
What?
Look!
But, Doctor, what can we do?
Well, I don't know. If we go down there, we'll bump straight into them.
I'm afraid they're trapped!
Thirty minutes from Deacon Alpha-3, sir.
Right. We want the figure to stand by on C-Day gear.
Right, sir.
Emergency from Deacon Alpha-4, sir.
The storm is being attacked.
Switch course via Alpha-4. Try to get me a visual on this carrier.
On course, sir.
Bridge to powerhouse. I want main boost for as long as you can hold it without vaporizing the motors.
This one's still alive.
So the Space Corps were too busy to bother about us, eh?
Shut up!
I'm thinking.
Well, there's no time for thinking. We've got to get out of here.
Four space cars and an officer. What are they doing here?
There must be a cruiser in the area.
Not a big enough crew to defend the beacon, but they must have been put aboard for a reason.
What's this?
It looks like a fixed beam transmitter.
Well, that's it.
Well, they'll be on their way back here by now.
Then you'd better get moving.
Well, you don't still want a beacon coming up.
That's what we came here to do.
Don't waste time. Get on with it.
Could be their radio's packed up, sir.
Yes.
You give me a projected arrival time.
Two hours, twenty minutes.
I should have left a stronger picket.
Oh, no, sir. We haven't the manpower.
Besides, Zorba knew he could only hope to delay things.
I am going to get that gang of murdering thieves if I have to spend the next ten years out here.
Yes, Lieutenant. You're the last of the toy soldiers.
Shut in the back.
You mean we're disqualified. You don't want to play any more.
I couldn't laugh now. But you won't get away with this.
Who's going to stop me, Lieutenant?
How did you get those decoys aboard?
Decoys?
The street that led us into your ambush.
Concussion, Lieutenant? Or stalling for time? Which?
You know what I'm talking about. They ran off into the off-companion way.
One of my men down there must be some of yours.
Sure. We were having a private training session with loaded filmite guns.
We did hear firing in the airlock.
You mean there really is someone else in there?
I thought you planted them there.
Whoever they are, I've got no time to bother with them now.
Blame the charges. Just fix him a rocket.
Good. Well, if he can walk, get him out of here. If he can't, leave him.
What are you doing?
Just sealing a coffin, dervish.
We should have seen what they were seeing.
I thought they were trying to burn through it.
Just a minute. I think they've got away.
I don't understand. Why didn't they come in here after us?
They must have known we were trapped.
Why not finish us off?
Didn't seem very friendly, did they?
Oh! What's the matter?
It's hot. You try.
No, thank you.
I told you they were trying to burn through it.
Why haven't they?
There's something moving out there.
Sounds as though somebody's on the hull.
What are they doing?
I don't know, Jamie. Perhaps they're cleaning the windows.
They?
Why don't we speak back to the Tardis and get out of here?
We've still got the chance.
Sensible idea, Zaria.
You sure there's nobody out there?
I haven't heard anybody for ages. Come on.
Then I'm out of the spot.
Well, it's not ours anymore.
What?
But I can't unlock it.
Oh, let me, Zoe.
We'll have to eat more porridge.
Jamie, I don't think it's any use.
You know what I think they've done?
What?
They've welded the lock. We're prisoners.
...beacon Alpha-4, sir.
Exactly what happened before.
What is our arrival time?
Still 90 minutes to go, sir.
We are going to be too late again.
The beacon should blow any second now.
